description: EMILE, Energy Monitoring in Less Effort, collects consumption readings across municipal assets. Its README lists Green Button XML from manual or connected utility routes and ordinary CSV as inputs, with graphs and CSV reports as outputs. Users map meter data to schools, offices or other local facilities and compare usage over time. Geographic coverage is the participating municipality and utility territory; the application is not a national meter dataset. GitHub metadata states MIT licensing for the software. A limitation is that different billing periods, estimated reads and property changes can distort apparent efficiency trends. An automatic utility connection can also require third-party credentials and consent. EMILE can prepare building-load baselines and retrofit evidence for city energy simulations. The related ERA5 catalogue record supplies weather conditions, which can help interpret usage but is not the aggregator. No utility bills, API keys or application build were downloaded.
name: EMILE municipal energy-data aggregator
